name: Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory

operator.value: Institute of High Energy Physics (IHEP), Chinese Academy of Sciences
operator.note: IHEP's press release identifies itself (as publisher) as the host institute for the JUNO experiment; no separate 'facility operator' statement was found distinct from the experiment/collaboration announcements.

intervals.label: conceptual design
intervals.quote: The Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) is proposed to determine the neutrino mass hierarchy using an underground liquid scintillator detector.

intervals.label: underground laboratory and detector installation
intervals.quote: Detector installation started in 2021 and completed in December 2024
intervals.locator: IHEP news, 2024-12-17 (via search-summarised extract; the fetched page itself confirms the final construction/filling stage began 2024-12-18)
intervals.note: The installation start year (2021) is drawn from a secondary IHEP-sourced search summary, not verbatim text seen in the fetched page; the fetched page (english.ihep.cas.cn, 2024-12-17) does independently confirm the final construction stage began 2024-12-18, which is used for the next interval.

intervals.label: final construction stage: water and liquid-scintillator filling
intervals.quote: The final stage of the construction of the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) began on Dec. 18
intervals.note: End date is the physics data-taking start date (2025-08-26), taken as the point commissioning/filling activity concluded.

intervals.label: operating as an underground laboratory
intervals.quote: JUNO began physics data taking on August 26, 2025

overburden.quote: The experimental hall, spanning more than 50 meters, is under a granite mountain of over 700 m overburden.

notes: This facility (the excavated underground laboratory beneath Dashi Hill, Kaiping, Jiangmen) is distinct from IHEP itself, which is the operating national laboratory; IHEP is recorded only via `operator` (S string), not as a separate facility record, per this wave's scope.
No approval date (between the 2015 CDR proposal and the 2021 start of detector installation) was found in a source fetched this session; the intervening years are not covered by a sourced interval.

summary.plain: A giant underground hall in southern China, dug into a hill near Jiangmen, that holds the JUNO neutrino detector deep beneath the rock so cosmic rays cannot swamp its measurements.
summary.technical: Underground laboratory beneath Dashi Hill, Kaiping, Jiangmen, Guangdong, China, with roughly 700 m of granite overburden, purpose-built to host the JUNO liquid-scintillator reactor-antineutrino detector 52.5 km from the Yangjiang and Taishan nuclear power plants.
